# Clausery

> Clausery is browser-based document automation. It turns ordinary Word (.docx) templates with {tags} into guided questionnaires and generates finished documents entirely on the user's device: no upload, no account, works offline. Free for up to three templates with unlimited documents; the Pro plan adds unlimited templates, calculations, an encrypted workspace and client intake forms.

Key facts:
- Documents are assembled in the browser; template files, answers and generated documents are never sent to a server.
- Templates are normal Word files. Tags: {name} for a value, {#condition}...{/condition} for optional text, {^condition}...{/condition} for the opposite, and {#list}...{/list} for repeating paragraphs or table rows.
- Pro plan: optional passphrase encryption of everything stored in the browser (AES-256-GCM) with auto-lock.
- Free Word templates, a contract clause library and free drafting tools are available without sign-up.
- Clausery is software, not a law firm, and does not give legal advice.

## Product
- [Home](https://getclausery.github.io/): what Clausery does and who it is for
- [Open the app](https://getclausery.github.io/app/): runs in the browser, no sign-up
- [Pricing](https://getclausery.github.io/pricing/): Free, Pro, Team and Enterprise plans
- [Security](https://getclausery.github.io/docs/security.html): how data stays on the device
- [Documentation](https://getclausery.github.io/docs/): getting started, template syntax, logic, client intake

## Contract clause library
- [Indemnification clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/indemnification-clause.html): Free sample indemnification clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An indemnity is a promise by one party to cover the other party's losses if a specified kind of claim arises, most often a claim by a third party caused by the first party's breach, negligence or infringement of someone else's intellectual property.
- [Limitation of liability clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/limitation-of-liability-clause.html): Free sample limitation of liability clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A limitation of liability clause caps how much one party can recover from the other, and usually excludes whole categories of loss, such as lost profits and indirect or consequential damages.
- [Force majeure clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/force-majeure-clause.html): Free sample force majeure clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A force majeure clause excuses a party from performing, for as long as an extraordinary event outside its control prevents it: natural disasters, war, epidemics, government orders and similar events.
- [Confidentiality clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/confidentiality-clause.html): Free sample confidentiality clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A confidentiality clause obliges a party to keep the other party's non-public information secret, use it only for the purpose of the contract, and share it only with people who need to know it.
- [Non-solicitation clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/non-solicitation-clause.html): Free sample non-solicitation clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A non-solicitation clause stops a party from actively approaching the other party's employees, contractors or customers for a period, usually during the contract and for a time after it ends.
- [Non-compete clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/non-compete-clause.html): Free sample non-compete clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A non-compete clause prevents a person or business from working for, or running, a competing business for a period and within an area after a relationship ends.
- [Payment terms clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/payment-terms-clause.html): Free sample payment terms clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. The payment terms clause says when a party can invoice, how long the other party has to pay, in what currency and by what method, and what happens when an invoice is disputed.
- [Late payment interest clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/late-payment-interest-clause.html): Free sample late payment interest clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A late payment clause lets the party that is owed money charge interest on overdue amounts, and often suspend work until it is paid.
- [Intellectual property assignment clause: sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/intellectual-property-clause.html): Free sample intellectual property assignment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An intellectual property clause decides who owns the copyright, designs, inventions and other rights in the work created under a contract, and what each side may do with the other's pre-existing material.
- [Warranty clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/warranty-clause.html): Free sample warranty clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A warranty is a contractual promise about a fact or about quality, such as that services will be performed with reasonable skill and care, or that software will work as specified for 90 days. The warranty clause also sets the remedy when the promise is broken.
- [Independent contractor clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/independent-contractor-clause.html): Free sample independent contractor clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. This clause records that a person is engaged as an independent business, not as an employee, and that they are responsible for their own taxes, insurance and working arrangements.
- [Termination for convenience clause: sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/termination-for-convenience-clause.html): Free sample termination for convenience clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A termination for convenience clause lets a party end the contract without giving any reason, usually on a period of written notice.
- [Termination for cause clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/termination-for-cause-clause.html): Free sample termination for cause clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A termination for cause clause lets a party end the contract when the other party commits a material breach and does not fix it in time, or becomes insolvent.
- [Survival clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/survival-clause.html): Free sample survival clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A survival clause lists the obligations that continue after a contract ends, such as confidentiality, payment, indemnities and limits on liability.
- [Governing law and jurisdiction clause: sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/governing-law-clause.html): Free sample governing law and jurisdiction clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A governing law clause chooses which country's or state's law applies to the contract. A jurisdiction clause chooses which courts will hear disputes about it. They are separate choices, usually placed together.
- [Dispute resolution clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/dispute-resolution-clause.html): Free sample dispute resolution clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A dispute resolution clause sets out the steps the parties must take when they disagree: usually negotiation between senior people first, then mediation, then arbitration or court.
- [Notices clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/notices-clause.html): Free sample notices clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A notices clause says how formal notices under the contract, such as notices of breach, renewal or termination, must be sent, to which address, and when they count as received.
- [Entire agreement clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/entire-agreement-clause.html): Free sample entire agreement clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An entire agreement clause, also called an integration or merger clause, says that the written contract contains everything the parties agreed, replacing earlier emails, proposals and conversations.
- [Severability clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/severability-clause.html): Free sample severability clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A severability clause says that if one part of the contract is invalid or unenforceable, the rest of the contract still stands, and the invalid part is trimmed or removed.
- [Assignment clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/assignment-clause.html): Free sample assignment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An assignment clause says whether a party can transfer its rights under the contract to someone else, for example when it sells its business, and on what conditions.
- [Amendment clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/amendment-clause.html): Free sample amendment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An amendment or variation clause says how the contract can be changed, usually only by a written document signed by both parties.
- [Waiver clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/waiver-clause.html): Free sample waiver clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A no-waiver clause says that if a party does not enforce a right straight away, for example by accepting a late payment without complaint, it has not given that right up.
- [Counterparts and electronic signature clause: sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/electronic-signature-clause.html): Free sample counterparts and electronic signature clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. A counterparts clause lets each party sign a separate copy of the contract, with all copies together forming one agreement. An electronic signature clause confirms the parties accept e-signatures and signed PDFs.
- [At-will employment clause: meaning and sample wording](https://getclausery.github.io/clauses/at-will-employment-clause.html): Free sample at-will employment clause wording, explained in plain English: what it does, what to check and common questions. An at-will clause states that either the employer or the employee can end the employment at any time, with or without cause or notice, as US law generally allows.

## Guides
- [How to automate a Word template without uploading it anywhere](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/automate-word-templates.html): A step-by-step guide to turning any Word document into a reusable, fill-in-the-blanks template with questions, conditional clauses and lists, entirely in your browser.
- [Conditional clauses in Word: include or remove paragraphs automatically](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/conditional-clauses-in-word.html): How to make parts of a Word document appear only when they apply: yes/no sections, either/or wording, clauses based on amounts or dates, and removing empty lines.
- [Client intake without a portal: collect answers by email, privately](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/client-intake-without-a-portal.html): How to send clients a questionnaire they can fill in offline and return as a file, so you can generate documents from their answers without a client portal or account.
- [Mail merge vs document automation: which one do you need?](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/mail-merge-vs-document-automation.html): Mail merge fills the same blanks from a spreadsheet; document automation also includes or removes clauses, repeats lists and calculates. How to tell which one your documents need.
- [Repeating lists and table rows in Word templates](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/repeating-lists-and-tables-in-word.html): How to make a Word template repeat a paragraph, bullet or table row for every party, attorney, deliverable or line item, with separators and numbering.
- [Choosing document software when client confidentiality matters: a checklist](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/confidentiality-checklist-document-software.html): Questions to ask before putting client or employee information into any document or drafting tool: where data is processed, who can access it, sub-processors, retention and exit.
- [How to write a job offer letter (with a free template)](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/how-to-write-an-offer-letter.html): What to put in a job offer letter: role, start date, pay, bonus, equity, benefits, conditions and at-will wording, plus the mistakes that cause disputes later.
- [How to write a demand letter for unpaid invoices](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/how-to-write-a-payment-demand-letter.html): A step-by-step guide to asking a customer for overdue payment in writing: what to include, tone, deadlines, interest, and what to do if they still do not pay.
- [What to include in a statement of work (SOW)](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/what-to-include-in-a-statement-of-work.html): The sections every statement of work needs: scope, deliverables, timeline, fees, assumptions, acceptance and change control, with examples of what goes wrong when they are missing.
- [What to include in an NDA: a clause-by-clause checklist](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/what-to-include-in-an-nda.html): The clauses a non-disclosure agreement needs, from the definition of confidential information to exclusions, term, return of information and governing law, and when to use a mutual or one-way NDA.
- [How to write a freelance contract: 10 clauses that prevent disputes](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/how-to-write-a-freelance-contract.html): What every freelance contract should say about scope, revisions, deadlines, payment, deposits, kill fees, ownership and termination, with free templates for designers, photographers, writers and more.
- [What is a kill fee? How to set one in a freelance contract](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/what-is-a-kill-fee.html): A kill fee is what a client pays if they cancel a freelance project after work has started. How much to charge, how to word it, and how it differs from a deposit.
- [What to do when a client won't pay: a step-by-step plan](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/what-to-do-when-a-client-wont-pay.html): A calm plan for an unpaid invoice: reminders, a final notice, late fees, a demand letter and small claims, with reminder emails you can copy.
- [Is an MOU legally binding? How it differs from a contract](https://getclausery.github.io/guides/is-an-mou-legally-binding.html): When a memorandum of understanding or letter of intent becomes a binding contract, how courts decide, and how to word yours so it binds only what you mean.

## Free tools
- [Amount in words converter for contracts and cheques](https://getclausery.github.io/free-tools/amount-in-words.html): Write any amount in words for contracts, cheques and promissory notes, such as "One Thousand Two Hundred and Fifty Dollars and 50/100".
- [Contract deadline calculator (business days, months, years)](https://getclausery.github.io/free-tools/deadline-calculator.html): Add or subtract days, business days, weeks, months or years from a date, with month-end handling and your own holidays.
- [Net 30 calculator: invoice due date for any payment terms](https://getclausery.github.io/free-tools/invoice-due-date.html): Find the due date for Net 30, Net 60, EOM, 15 MFI or 2/10 net 30 invoices, the days left to pay and what an early payment discount is worth.
- [Late payment interest calculator (contract or UK statutory)](https://getclausery.github.io/free-tools/late-payment-interest.html): Work out interest on an overdue invoice at your contract rate, or UK statutory interest at 8% above base rate plus the fixed compensation sum.
- [Freelance rate calculator: hourly and day rate](https://getclausery.github.io/free-tools/freelance-rate.html): Work back from the income you want to keep to the hourly and day rate you need to charge, after tax, costs and time off.
- [Loan repayment calculator with amortization schedule](https://getclausery.github.io/free-tools/loan-repayment.html): Work out the payment on a loan repaid in equal instalments, the total interest and a full repayment schedule with dates, for weekly to yearly payments.
- [Word template tag checker](https://getclausery.github.io/free-tools/template-checker.html): Check a .docx template for broken {tags} and see the questionnaire it would produce. The file never leaves your computer.

## Comparisons
- [Gavel alternative that keeps client data on your computer](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/gavel-alternative.html): Gavel is a well-regarded cloud platform for legal document automation and client workflows. Clausery does the core job, turning Word templates into guided questionnaires, without sending client data to a vendor.
- [Clio Draft alternative for firms that cannot upload client files](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/clio-draft-alternative.html): Clio Draft (formerly Lawyaw) is document automation that lives inside the Clio ecosystem. Clausery is independent of any practice management system and never uploads the documents it builds.
- [HotDocs alternative: lightweight document automation in the browser](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/hotdocs-alternative.html): HotDocs has been a standard for enterprise document assembly for decades. Clausery is a much lighter tool: no installation, no server, and no component library to learn, for firms that need the essentials.
- [docassemble alternative that needs no server](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/docassemble-alternative.html): docassemble is a powerful, free, open-source platform for guided interviews, widely used in access-to-justice projects. It runs on a server you host. Clausery runs in the browser with nothing to install or host.
- [LawDepot alternative with free Word downloads](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/lawdepot-alternative.html): LawDepot charges to print or download after a 7-day trial. Clausery's templates download free as Word files you fill in on your computer. An honest comparison.
- [Rocket Lawyer alternative: free templates, no membership](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/rocket-lawyer-alternative.html): Rocket Lawyer bundles documents with attorney help in a membership. If you only need the documents, Clausery's Word templates are free. An honest comparison.
- [eForms alternative: fill in documents without an account](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/eforms-alternative.html): eForms has free blank forms and paid plans after a 7-day trial. Clausery fills in its free templates in your browser, with no account, card or trial.
- [HoneyBook alternative when you only need contracts](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/honeybook-alternative.html): Only use HoneyBook for contracts? Clausery has free Word contract templates you fill in on your own computer. An honest comparison of features and price.
- [Bonsai alternative: free freelance contracts in Word](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/bonsai-alternative.html): Only use Bonsai for contracts? Get free freelance contracts in Word, filled in on your own computer. An honest comparison of features, price and trade-offs.
- [Dubsado alternative: contracts without the setup](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/dubsado-alternative.html): Dubsado is powerful but slow to set up. If you mainly need contracts, Clausery takes you from a Word template to a finished contract in minutes, for free.
- [PandaDoc alternative for Word contract templates](https://getclausery.github.io/compare/pandadoc-alternative.html): Compare PandaDoc with Clausery for Word contract templates: guided questionnaires, .docx output, no per-seat pricing and no upload. Honest trade-offs.
